feed.title: Economics & Finance — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Awesome AI in Finance
entry.summary: A list of tools, data and papers solving finance problems with machine learning. Unlike general finance lists it focuses on the AI intersection.

entry.title: Awesome Algorand
entry.summary: A list of developer resources for Algorand, a proof-of-stake blockchain.

entry.title: Awesome Billing
entry.summary: A list of engineering resources for payments, invoicing, pricing and accounting.

entry.title: Awesome Bitcoin
entry.summary: A list of services and tools for Bitcoin software development.

entry.title: Awesome Bitcoin Payment Processors
entry.summary: A list of processors and tools to start accepting Bitcoin payments.

entry.title: Awesome Coins
entry.summary: A list of cryptocurrency tools and algorithms — wallets, node software, libraries. Unlike price sites it collects the underlying technology, not the product.

entry.title: Awesome Cosmos
entry.summary: A resource list for Cosmos, a modular framework for building app-specific blockchains.

entry.title: Awesome Credit Modeling
entry.summary: A list of methods for classifying credit applicants and modelling risk.

entry.title: Awesome Ethereum
entry.summary: A list of developer resources for Ethereum, the smart-contract platform.

entry.title: Awesome Ledger
entry.summary: A resource list for double-entry accounting on the command line (Ledger).

entry.title: Awesome Stock Trading
entry.summary: A collection of libraries, strategies and data sources for stock trading. Not investment advice; a list of the tooling in one place.

entry.title: BIS — Bank for International Settlements
entry.summary: The central bank of central banks; publishes global financial statistics and research papers.

entry.title: CoinGecko
entry.summary: Market data for thousands of crypto assets with broad coverage including DEXes and a free API.

entry.title: CoinMarketCap
entry.summary: Widely used crypto prices and rankings, providing the canonical market-cap listing.

entry.title: DefiLlama
entry.summary: DeFi total-value-locked analytics across chains with an open, unbiased methodology and no token of its own.

entry.title: Dune
entry.summary: An analytics platform where the community builds dashboards with SQL queries over blockchain data.

entry.title: EconJobMarket
entry.summary: A platform managing academic economics job applications in one place, collecting applications and reference letters. A standard application flow instead of scattered emails.

entry.title: EconLib
entry.summary: A library holding an economics encyclopedia, essays and full texts of classic economics works.

entry.title: Economics Stack Exchange
entry.summary: An economics Q&A site where you can ask experts about concepts and models. Unlike a forum, voting and editing surface the best answer.

entry.title: Etherscan
entry.summary: Ethereum's canonical block explorer, with transaction tracing, contract verification and an API.

entry.title: Finviz
entry.summary: A visual stock screener that scans the US market on one screen with a heatmap and dense filters.

entry.title: FRED
entry.summary: The St. Louis Fed’s economic database — 800,000+ US and world series, with charting and an API. Unlike raw statistical releases, the browse-plot-download flow lives in one place.

entry.title: Glassnode
entry.summary: Crypto market intelligence through on-chain metrics and derived indicators.

entry.title: IDEAS / RePEc
entry.summary: The largest database of economics publications — over two million papers, working papers and software items. Unlike Google Scholar it is field-specific: it indexes economics alone and derives author and institution rankings.

entry.title: IGM Experts Panel
entry.summary: A panel where leading economists vote whether they agree with topical policy questions. Unlike a single expert’s view it shows at a glance where the consensus sits.

entry.title: IMF Data
entry.summary: The IMF’s macro data — the standard reference for balance of payments, exchange rates and debt. It leans more to monetary and fiscal statistics than the World Bank.

entry.title: Investing.com
entry.summary: Multi-asset real-time quotes together with an economic calendar in broad coverage.

entry.title: Investopedia
entry.summary: A beginner-oriented encyclopedia that explains finance and investing terms dictionary-style with worked examples.

entry.title: JOE · Job Openings for Economists
entry.summary: The American Economic Association’s official job board — the central place for the academic economics market. Unlike general job sites it is economics positions only.

entry.title: Khan Academy · Ekonomi
entry.summary: A free video-and-exercise set teaching the basics of micro, macro and finance from scratch. Unlike university courses it targets the introductory level and intuition.

entry.title: Koyfin
entry.summary: Bloomberg-like analytics dashboards for equities and macro, offered with a generous free tier.

entry.title: Macrotrends
entry.summary: Free long-term charts of stocks and economic data going back decades.

entry.title: Marginal Revolution
entry.summary: Tyler Cowen and Alex Tabarrok’s daily economics blog — among the most-read in the field. Against news it offers a short, frequent stream of commentary through an economist’s lens.

entry.title: Messari
entry.summary: Research-grade profiles, governance data and reports for crypto assets.

entry.title: MIT OCW · İktisat
entry.summary: Over 100 courses across every major field of economics in MIT’s open courseware. Unlike YouTube playlists these are full course structures with prerequisites and reading lists.

entry.title: Musings on Markets (Aswath Damodaran)
entry.summary: Valuation professor Damodaran's writing and free datasets, an authoritative source on valuation frameworks.

entry.title: Nasdaq Data Link (Quandl)
entry.summary: A service aggregating financial and economic data from many sources under one API (formerly Quandl). Instead of pulling scattered sources one by one, you get them through a common interface.

entry.title: NBER Working Papers
entry.summary: Working papers from the US National Bureau of Economic Research — most later appear in peer-reviewed journals. You read the field’s leading research here before the journals.

entry.title: OECD Data
entry.summary: Official OECD statistics across member economies, standardised for cross-country comparison straight from the source.

entry.title: OpenStax · Principles of Economics
entry.summary: A free, openly licensed textbook for introductory university economics. Unlike commercial texts it is free and regularly updated, with PDF, web and print editions.
